title: A Three-Point Continuous-Variable Quantum MacWilliams Identity
abstract: We construct the three-point continuous-variable (CV) quantum MacWilliams identity, extending the two-point framework of Burchards, and give its closed-form integral kernel. Its configuration space carries a symplectic invariant with no classical counterpart, which encodes the GKP quantization condition and a three-point sign phase. Using the identity, we derive the semidefinite-programming bounds it supports on the dimension of CV quantum error-correcting codes, and we prove, in two collapse theorems, that the three-point apparatus does not improve on the two-point bound. For GKP lattice codes the three-point optimum equals the Burchards two-point linear-programming optimum identically. This is an exact determination of the lattice three-point optimum, so the $E_8$ and Leech magic functions saturate it rather than beat it. For general bosonic codes a completely-positive reformulation bypasses the positivity obstruction that rules out the natural factored-form constructions; the phase-sign condition together with Choi positivity then force the three-point term to vanish. We certify this collapse for radial Choi forms on the first eight Laguerre levels at one mode, and leave the full trace-class cone open. Both collapses have a single cause with no classical analogue, the code projector: it orients the bound correctly but also removes the full positivity that powers the classical three-point improvement.
summary: This paper develops a three-point continuous-variable quantum MacWilliams identity for bosonic error-correcting codes. It uses advanced techniques involving characteristic functions and SDPs to derive bounds on code dimension. The key finding is that this sophisticated three-point bound collapses back to the established two-point bound for important classes of codes, providing deep structural insight into the limitations of current QEC theory.
main_problem: The authors construct a three-point continuous-variable (CV) quantum MacWilliams identity to derive tighter semidefinite-programming (SDP) bounds on the dimension of CV quantum error-correcting codes.
main_result: They prove that for GKP lattice codes, the three-point bound does not improve upon the existing two-point linear-programming optimum; furthermore, general bosonic code analysis shows a collapse to the two-point bound due to structural constraints imposed by the code projector.
method: The work involves constructing and analyzing complex integral kernels (the three-point identity) using characteristic functions derived from displacement operators, followed by rigorous SDP bounding techniques and positive-definiteness proofs in exact arithmetic.
model_or_system: The system studied is bosonic quantum error-correcting codes, particularly those based on the Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill (GKP) construction within an infinite-dimensional harmonic oscillator Hilbert space. The analysis focuses on weight distributions over the configuration space of Gram matrices.
key_observables: Code dimension ($K$), protection distance ($d$), and the minimum eigenvalue ($\lambda_{\min}$) of positive combination matrices $P(\mu)$ used as SDP certificates.
important_parameters: The lattice structure (GKP), the number of modes ($N$), and the truncation level ($M$) are key parameters governing the bounds and analysis complexity.
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on an envelope-cut approximation ($\sigma > 0$) for physical realization, and certain structural assumptions about the form of the weight distributions ($A_3$ and $B_3$).
figures_summary: Figures/tables summarize calculated values for admissibility distances and ratios comparing different bounding techniques (e.g., $ho_N = K_{ne}/K_{Lev}$), confirming theoretical bounds.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the construction of the three-point identity kernel, through deriving its relationship to known two-point identities via BCH expansion, and culminates in proving the non-improvement of this bound for specific code types using SDP techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical constraints on quantum error correction codes beyond simple stabilizer assumptions, linking algebraic structures (MacWilliams identities) directly to fundamental physical limitations imposed by positivity.
